questions.text: Which cost category is expressly excluded from Project Construction Cost (PCC) under SPP Document 202 Section 7.17?

options.text: Mechanical and electrical building systems
The Architect, Engineer, and Specialist Consultant fees
Fire protection and alarm systems
Materials and labor for installation

rationale.a: These building systems are listed within PCC when planned and designed for the project.
rationale.b: SPP 202 Section 7.17 excludes the fees of the Architect, Engineer, and Specialist Consultants from PCC.
rationale.c: These systems are listed within PCC when part of the completed building.
rationale.d: Materials and labor for installation are expressly part of PCC.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 Section 7.17 excludes the fees of the Architect, Engineer, and Specialist Consultants from PCC.
rationale.takeaway: PCC is the completed-building construction cost base, not a container for professional fees.

questions.text: Which item is included in PCC when it is planned and designed by the Architect or consultants?

options.text: The Architect fee being computed from PCC
Construction inspector salaries
The completed building systems indicated in the plans and specifications
Owner financing cost for the project site

rationale.a: The Architect fee is excluded from PCC.
rationale.b: Construction inspector salaries are excluded from PCC.
rationale.c: SPP 202 Section 7.17 includes building systems and items indicated in the Architect and consultant plans, designs, drawings, and specifications.
rationale.d: Financing cost belongs outside PCC; project development cost is broader than PCC.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 Section 7.17 includes building systems and items indicated in the Architect and consultant plans, designs, drawings, and specifications.
rationale.takeaway: Classify the item by whether it is part of the completed building work.

questions.text: Why does PCC matter in percentage-of-PCC compensation?

options.text: It is the construction-cost base to which the percentage fee is applied
It fixes the contractor profit margin
It replaces all Owner-Architect payment milestones
It includes land, permits, utilities, and financing cost

rationale.a: The SPP states that percentage compensation is based on PCC and defines PCC as the completed-building construction cost.
rationale.b: PCC does not set contractor profit by itself.
rationale.c: Payment milestones are handled separately in the Owner-Architect Agreement.
rationale.d: Those broader items belong to project development cost, not PCC.
rationale.correct: The SPP states that percentage compensation is based on PCC and defines PCC as the completed-building construction cost.
rationale.takeaway: Do not confuse PCC with the Owner total project budget.

questions.text: If the Owner furnishes material below market cost, how should that material be treated for PCC?

options.text: Exclude it entirely because the Owner supplied it
Use only the discounted purchase amount
Compute the material and labor on current fair market value
Add the Architect fee to offset the discount

rationale.a: SPP 202 does not exclude owner-furnished material simply because the Owner supplied it.
rationale.b: SPP 202 rejects an artificially low amount when market value is higher.
rationale.c: SPP 202 Section 7.17 says owner-furnished labor or material below market cost is still computed on current fair market value.
rationale.d: Professional fees are excluded from the PCC base.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 Section 7.17 says owner-furnished labor or material below market cost is still computed on current fair market value.
rationale.takeaway: The fair-market rule prevents an artificial reduction of the construction-cost base.

questions.text: Which statement best distinguishes PCC from Project Development Cost?

options.text: PCC includes professional fees and site acquisition cost
PCC is narrower; Project Development Cost includes construction plus professional fees, permits, utilities, land, and cost of money
Both terms have the same scope under SPP 202
Project Development Cost excludes construction cost

rationale.a: Those broader items are not all PCC.
rationale.b: SPP 202 defines Project Development Cost as broader than PCC because it includes construction plus professional fees, permits, utilities, land, cost of money, and similar items.
rationale.c: The SPP defines Project Development Cost separately from PCC.
rationale.d: Project Development Cost includes construction cost plus other items.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 defines Project Development Cost as broader than PCC because it includes construction plus professional fees, permits, utilities, land, cost of money, and similar items.
rationale.takeaway: Use PCC for the completed-building construction base; use Project Development Cost for the broader owner-side project cost concept.

questions.text: Which source-backed statement about cost estimates is safest?

options.text: The Architect guarantees every SPPCC amount
The Architect does not guarantee SPPCC or cost estimates because labor, material, and bidding costs are outside the Architect control
Design Development estimates are always within a fixed percentage band
Contract Documents estimates are always exact

rationale.a: UAP Document 401-402 Article 9 says the Architect does not guarantee estimate accuracy.
rationale.b: UAP Document 401-402 Article 9 states that the Architect does not guarantee SPPCC or cost estimate accuracy because cost factors are outside the Architect control.
rationale.c: The checked source does not provide fixed estimate accuracy bands.
rationale.d: The checked source rejects guaranteed accuracy.
rationale.correct: UAP Document 401-402 Article 9 states that the Architect does not guarantee SPPCC or cost estimate accuracy because cost factors are outside the Architect control.
rationale.takeaway: Avoid unsourced accuracy bands unless a source is attached.

questions.text: When the Schematic Design phase is completed, what cost document is submitted under the checked SPP/Agreement language?

options.text: Statement of Probable Project Construction Cost based on current cost parameters
Final Project Construction Cost based on completion records
A guaranteed bid price
A land acquisition budget

rationale.a: The SPP and UAP Document 401-402 both describe an SPPCC submitted during early design service stages.
rationale.b: Final PCC is not established at schematic design.
rationale.c: The source says probable cost, not guaranteed bid price.
rationale.correct: The SPP and UAP Document 401-402 both describe an SPPCC submitted during early design service stages.
rationale.takeaway: SPPCC is a probable construction-cost statement, not a guarantee.

questions.text: Which item should not be added to PCC when computing the Architect fee base?

options.text: Elevators planned and designed for the project
Mechanical equipment indicated in the plans
Construction inspector salaries
Architectural interiors planned by the Architect

rationale.a: Elevators are listed within PCC when part of the project.
rationale.b: Mechanical equipment is listed within PCC.
rationale.c: SPP 202 Section 7.17 excludes salaries of construction inspectors from PCC.
rationale.d: Architectural interiors planned and designed by the Architect are part of PCC.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 Section 7.17 excludes salaries of construction inspectors from PCC.
rationale.takeaway: The exclusion list is as important as the inclusion list.

questions.text: At completion, what does UAP Document 401-402 say the Owner furnishes to the Architect?

options.text: Two copies of the summary of all construction labor, services, materials, equipment, fixtures, and items used for completion
A waiver of the Architect fee
A new SPPCC replacing all previous agreements
The Architect personal tax return

rationale.a: UAP Document 401-402 Article 10 requires the Owner to furnish records and a completion summary of construction costs/items.
rationale.b: The source does not require a waiver of the Architect fee.
rationale.c: The completion record is not a new SPPCC replacing the contract.
rationale.d: The source discusses project cost records, not tax returns.
rationale.correct: UAP Document 401-402 Article 10 requires the Owner to furnish records and a completion summary of construction costs/items.
rationale.takeaway: Cost records support final project cost reconciliation.

questions.text: A board item lists land, professional fees, permits, utilities, and cost of money. Which source term best fits that broader basket?

options.text: Project Construction Cost only
Project Development Cost
Construction inspector salary exclusion
MDPE multiplier

rationale.a: PCC is narrower and excludes professional fees.
rationale.b: SPP 202 Section 7.18 defines Project Development Cost as including construction plus professional fees, permits, utilities, land, and cost of money.
rationale.c: This describes an exclusion, not the whole basket.
rationale.d: MDPE is a compensation method, not the broader project cost basket.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 Section 7.18 defines Project Development Cost as including construction plus professional fees, permits, utilities, land, and cost of money.
rationale.takeaway: When land and financing appear, the question is usually broader than PCC.
